title: "10. Staged progression: K stays 1×1 while K_L grows"

## Overview

The staged-progression model (van den Driessche & Watmough 2002, section 4.3) has `n`
infectious stages in series, each with its own infectivity `βₖ` and progression rate
`νₖ`. All infections enter stage 1, so whatever `n` is, the next-generation matrix `K` is
`1 × 1` and `R₀` is a sum over stages, whereas the large-domain matrix `K_L` is `n × n`.
This vignette builds the model for arbitrary `n` with array symbolics.

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

function staged_model(n)
    @parameters β[1:n] ν[1:n] d N
    @variables S(t) I(t)[1:n]
    βv, νv, Iv = collect(β), collect(ν), collect(I)
    λ = S * sum(βv[k] * Iv[k] for k in 1:n) / N
    eqs = [D(S) ~ -λ, D(Iv[1]) ~ λ - (νv[1] + d) * Iv[1]]
    for k in 2:n
        push!(eqs, D(Iv[k]) ~ νv[k - 1] * Iv[k - 1] - (νv[k] + d) * Iv[k])
    end
    sys = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :staged))
    return sys, S, Iv, βv, νv, d, N
end
sys, S, Iv, βv, νv, d, N = staged_model(4)
ngm = next_generation_matrix(sys, Iv; equilibrium = Dict(S => N))
```

## Large and restricted domains

```{julia}
size(ngm.K_L), size(ngm.K), states_at_infection(ngm)
```

`-Σ⁻¹` is lower triangular: the expected time spent in stage `k` by someone now in stage
`j ≤ k` is the probability of reaching `k` times the mean stay there.

```{julia}
mean_sojourn_times(ngm)
```

```{julia}
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

This is equation (4.4) of van den Driessche & Watmough:

```{julia}
paper = sum(βv[k] * prod(νv[j] for j in 1:(k - 1); init = 1) / prod(νv[j] + d for j in 1:k)
for k in 1:4)
symbolic_isequal(R0, paper)
```

## Which stage drives transmission?

Elasticities with respect to the stage infectivities are the fractions of `R₀` contributed
by each stage:

```{julia}
vals = Dict{Any, Any}(d => 0.01, N => 1.0)
for k in 1:4
    vals[βv[k]] = [0.1, 0.5, 0.3, 0.05][k]
    vals[νv[k]] = [0.5, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1][k]
end
e = elasticities(ngm, vals; params = βv)
[e[βv[k]] for k in 1:4]
```

```{julia}
sum(e[βv[k]] for k in 1:4)
```
